briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. We will now begin the climate briefing for October 28, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Accelerating Climate Crisis and Human Health Emergency
sections.content: According to The Lancet report, climate change is a 'global health emergency,' and its impacts are rapidly accelerating [57, 58, 88, 91]. Notably, as heatwave-related deaths reach an all-time high, 146 experts are urging the declaration of climate change as a global health emergency [59, 78, 82]. Such climate change is having a massive impact on human health and the economy, including causing $1 trillion in economic losses due to heatwaves [1, 2, 11]. Global research indicates that nearly 3 million climate change-related deaths have occurred, further highlighting its severity [87].

sections.title: ⚠️ Record-Breaking Greenhouse Gas Levels and Challenges for the International Community
sections.content: According to reports from the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) and the United Nations, greenhouse gas concentrations have reached an all-time high and are projected to accelerate further in 2025 [3, 12, 13, 98]. In this regard, a UN report pointed to the United States as one of the major reasons for the retreat in climate change response, revealing difficulties in international cooperation [62, 77]. Furthermore, climate change is causing extreme environmental shifts such as the disappearance of glaciers on Slovenia's highest peak [94] and the 30-year consecutive shrinkage of the Greenland ice sheet [97], with the first evidence of atmospheric methane changes due to wildfires also confirmed [71]. The policy directions of major countries are significantly impacting climate crisis response, as exemplified by former President Donald Trump's announcement of the 'termination' of the Biden administration's methane emission regulations [93] [86].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic Climate Change Response and Carbon Neutrality Transition Efforts
sections.content: Domestically, various efforts are underway to address the climate crisis and transition to carbon neutrality. Jeju Island is soliciting proposals for two 'Carbon Neutral Leading Villages' worth 11.2 billion KRW, establishing a locally-led carbon reduction model [17, 19, 20, 21, 27]. In Gurye County, the '2026 Carbon Neutral Soil Revitalization Expo' was successfully held [28]. Furthermore, adaptation efforts are also active: Hwaseong City is fostering kiwi cultivation as a regional strategic crop to respond to climate change [7], and Jinju City is preparing for seasonal changes and climate change by strengthening tap water management [6]. Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City and Paju City are also leveraging climate crisis response as an opportunity for regional growth by concretizing industrial carbon neutrality strategies and finalizing citizen-led '10 Carbon Neutrality Pledges,' respectively [26, 30].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Expansion of Renewable Energy and Dual Aspects of Infrastructure Development
sections.content: In the renewable energy sector, positive advancements coexist with challenges that need to be addressed. In the United States, renewable energy installed capacity has entered the 550 GW era [33]. Domestically, large-scale investments are continuing, with Shinhan Bank investing 250 billion KRW in renewable energy and community profit-sharing funds [37, 38, 41, 43, 50]. Notably, Gwangju Metropolitan City and Amkor have signed an RE100 renewable energy support agreement, accelerating companies' transition to carbon neutrality [44, 46]. Mohat has secured 2,625 rooftop solar power plants nationwide, achieving 110 billion KRW in power generation revenue [48, 53]. However, discussions about bottlenecks and overreach are being raised regarding the achievement of the 100 GW renewable energy capacity target [35, 42]. Furthermore, with projections indicating a decrease in global clean energy capacity additions this year [99], the importance of stable infrastructure development and policy support is highlighted.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing once again reminds us of the severity of the climate crisis and the urgent need for diverse global and domestic efforts. This concludes today's climate briefing.
